system.summary: Numbers 1 to about 240, each under one of nine marks above it (none, one bar, two bars, three dots, 'm', bar with a small circle, backward stroke, two strokes, bar and two dots); the same number under another mark is another group. Values are Spanish words, names, syllables and single letters in one list with homophones, in no alphabetical order. Identified (inference) with the decoding table TNA SP 106/6 no. 34 described by Tomokiyo, the cipher of Williamson's informants for Spanish papers.
system.sibling_key: Rebuilt from the period interlinear gloss of ff. 189r and 260r-v (key/table_v1.tsv); the period table SP 106/6 no. 34 not seen
system.notes: distinct_symbols = distinct number-and-mark groups in all transcriptions (about 10,600 groups), from the first reader's count (NOTES.md section 2), not re-measured. Single letters also occur among the values.

prior_solution.where: Period interlinear decipherment on ff. 187 (lines 1-5), 189, 243 (lines 1-4), 260, 264 and 294 (used for the key and Test A); the period decoding table SP 106/6 no. 34 at Kew (Tomokiyo; DECRYPT R510), not seen. No decipherment of the bare items found on the leaves or in print.

conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling saved the images on site at the Library of Congress and set the task and the rules; AI agents transcribed, rebuilt the key, tested, decoded and checked print. No person checked the transcriptions or readings.
models: Claude (Anthropic), Opus: transcriptions (two blind passes per item), key, tests, decoding, extension, print and literature checks
Claude (Anthropic), Opus 5.5: independent verifier (blind sample of 140 groups, rerun of both tests, Dumont check)

solution.what: Andrew Beling saved the State Papers Online images of the SP 84/165 cipher items on site at the Library of Congress (licensed; not included).
Two blind transcriptions each of the fully glossed letters ff. 189r and 260r-v (numerals agreeing 99.6% and 98.8%) and one of every other item; later a blind second pass of the five items read.
Key rebuilt from the period interlinear gloss of ff. 189 and 260 only (gloss aligned to groups by program, corrected line by line): 355 settled groups, frozen by sha256 before any test.
Test A, plan written first: the frozen table predicts the period gloss of ff. 264, 294 and the glossed openings of ff. 187, 243 at 83.7% (970 of 1,159); 200 shuffled tables at most 26.5%. Pass.

Test B, plan written first: coverage at least 45% and a Spanish trigram score above all 200 shuffled tables. Five of nine bare items pass (ff. 187, 245, 231, 313, 317); four have coverage 69-78% but 1-5 shuffles scoring as high and are 'not shown' (ff. 243r-244r, 244v, 306, 315). French control 10% coverage.
ff. 245r-v identified as a Spanish translation of the separate article of the Franco-Dutch treaty of 27 April 1662 printed by Dumont (VI.2 pp. 418-419); 20 extension values taken from the French.
47 extension groups in all (7 from glosses, 20 from the crib, 20 from context alone), marked and frozen separately (key/extension_v1.tsv).

Five items decoded from two passes each: 66-76% of groups firm from the frozen table, 3-10% extension, 13-22% unread. Holes in most sentences: decoded, not read. ff. 245r-v joined into a text against Dumont with every supplied word marked.

Tomokiyo (Cryptiana: SP 106/6 no. 34, DECRYPT R510); TNA catalogue of SP 84/165; Internet Archive and HathiTrust full text, CODOIN index vols. 1-61, Paz's Simancas catalogues: none of the letters in print. Refused: Google Books (429), Biblioteca Digital Hispanica (403), Biblioteca Virtual del Patrimonio Bibliografico (429).

Verifier, rule and marks written first: 80 bare groups transcribed blind agree with the two passes at 86-89% (number and mark; mark 85%); all 42 that the frozen table resolves give the same word. 60 glossed groups: numbers 58/60 the same, but the verifier's own per-group gloss attachment agreed with the table in 28/60 against a mark of 80% (a miss, from shifts in its alignment; all ten runs decode to the gloss over them, counted afterwards). Tests A and B rerun: identical. Treaty article: 9 of 17 named items from the frozen table alone against a mark of 10 (a near miss); 14 with the crib-based extension.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 3387 tokens, 295 types, es-golden-age order 4: reading -1.891 per letter; random keys -2.809 (z 11.0); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.011 (mean -2.041, z 9.2); annealer on the real text -2.028. Verdict: pass.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py, model es-golden-age) of the frozen-table decode of the five items (pass 2; extension left out): 3,387 read tokens, 295 types; reading -1.891 per letter; random keys -2.809 (z 11.0); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.011 (mean -2.041, z 9.2); annealer on the real text -2.028. Verdict: pass. It tests the frozen table's values on these items, not the words of a reading.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -1.891; polyphony 0.0; 1284 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.028

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Key rebuilt from the period interlinear decipherment of two sibling letters in the same volume (ff. 189, 260) and tested on four other glossed letters; not an independent solution. Extended from the printed French text of a treaty article (Dumont) and from context.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Groups, not words: firm (frozen table, both passes agree) 3,321 of 4,719 groups in the five decoded items (70%); extension 264; unread or disputed the rest (NOTES.md section 6). No item reaches a reading.

texts.label: ff. 245r-v, Spanish translation of the Franco-Dutch separate article of 27 April 1662
texts.summary: The separate article on France's duty of fifty sols a ton on foreign ships: equality under article 20 of the treaty does not exempt Dutch ships; they pay once a voyage, on leaving port, salt ships half; dated Paris, 27 April 1662; signatories in syllables.
texts.note: Decoded with the frozen table and the extension; holes in most sentences. Gist in NOTES.md section 6.

texts.label: ff. 187r-188r, Philip IV to Fuente, Aranjuez 26 April 1662, with his letter of 13 April and one to Gamarra
texts.summary: Spain to seek inclusion in the Franco-Dutch league; Fuente in Paris and Gamarra at The Hague to work together; a consul for Middelburg in Zeeland.
texts.note: Decoded with the frozen table and the extension; holes in most sentences. Gist in NOTES.md section 6.

texts.label: f. 231r-v, [Gamarra] to [Fuente], [May] 1662
texts.summary: English news (the Duke of York, a tax on chimneys, an oath refused by preachers) and the Anglo-Dutch treaty talks; the States to fit out twenty frigates against privateers.
texts.note: Decoded with the frozen table and the extension; holes in most sentences. Gist in NOTES.md section 6.

texts.label: ff. 313r-314r, [Gamarra] to the King, 1662
texts.summary: Little news; the league Gamarra has been ordered to further, the States of Holland, the Brandenburg resident, letters from Paris.
texts.note: Decoded with the frozen table and the extension; holes in most sentences. Gist in NOTES.md section 6.

texts.label: ff. 317r-318v, Fuente to the King, Paris, 1662
texts.summary: Fuente's protests over a French act on the Flanders frontier and an arret; the Count of Brienne and his son; arbitration under the treaties since Cateau-Cambresis.
texts.note: Decoded with the frozen table and the extension; holes in most sentences. Gist in NOTES.md section 6.
